item.title: ‘It All Comes to Roost at The Same Time’: Peter Frampton Talks New Doc, Album and Future Releases
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome to this week's music update. We're shining the spotlight on British-born rocker Peter Frampton, who's having a moment right now. With a new album and a documentary premiering, it's a great time to be a Frampton fan.
[Music transition]
Host: Peter Frampton just released his 19th studio album, "Carry The Light", his first album of all-new songs in 16 years. And if that's not enough, he's also premiering a new documentary, "Frampton", at the Tribeca Festival in New York this week. The documentary, directed by longtime band member Rob Arthur, explores Frampton's life and career, including his recent diagnosis with a degenerative disorder that's slowly limiting his mobility.
[Music transition]
Host: All of this comes just a few months after celebrating the 50th anniversary of "Frampton Comes Alive!", the iconic concert set that topped the Billboard 200 for 10 weeks back in 1976. We spoke with Peter Frampton himself, who says it's all happening at the same time, but he's excited to share these new projects with his fans.
[Clip of Peter Frampton speaking]
Host: The documentary was Rob Arthur's idea, who wanted to capture Frampton's story before it was too late. Arthur started filming during Frampton's Finale - The Farewell Tour in 2019 and ended up with a much bigger story than he initially planned.
[Music transition]
Host: With "Carry The Light" and the documentary "Frampton" out now, there's plenty to talk about. We'll be keeping an eye on Peter Frampton's latest projects, and we can't wait to see what's next for this rock legend.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's all for this week. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you in the next one.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
